rules.perspective: second person, with first person for the author's own observations
rules.formality: plain and direct, like a coach talking to one client across a desk
rules.humor: light and dry, at most once per chapter
rules.lists_vs_prose: prose by default; numbered steps only for a procedure the reader follows

signature_moves.chapter_openers: start inside a specific moment the reader recognizes
signature_moves.action_steps: one step, sized to finish in under 30 minutes, stated as an instruction
signature_moves.examples: name the person, the situation, what they did, and what happened

samples.title: Fixture sample
samples.text: You do not need a bigger network. You need a smaller list that you actually use. Most people I work with have three hundred contacts and talk to six of them. That is not a networking problem. It is a routine problem, and routines are fixable. Pick five names. Write them on a card. Put the card where you will see it on Friday at nine. That is the whole first step, and it takes four minutes.
